cues.en: If you put a colorful image into Photoshop or Instagram and blur it, you'll see a weird dark boundary between adjacent bright colors.
cues.zh: 如果你把一张色彩鲜艳的图片放入 Photoshop 或 Instagram 并对其进行模糊处理，你会发现在相邻的亮色之间有一条奇怪的暗色边界。

cues.en: In the real world, out of focus colors blend smoothly going from red to yellow to green, not red to brown brown to green. This color blending problem isn't limited to digital photo blurring either. Pretty much anytime a computer blurs an image or tries to use transparent edges, you'll see the same hideous sludge.
cues.zh: 在现实世界中，失焦的颜色会平滑地融合，从红到黄再到绿，而不是从红变成褐棕色再到绿。这种颜色融合的问题不仅限于数字照片模糊。几乎在任何时候，只要计算机模糊图像或试图使用透明边缘，你都会看到同样可怕的污浊感。

cues.en: There's a very simple explanation for this ugliness and a simple way to fix it. It all starts with how we perceive brightness.
cues.zh: 这种难看现象背后有一个非常简单的解释，也有一个简单的解决方法。这一切都始于我们对亮度的感知。

cues.en: Human vision, like our hearing, works on a relative and roughly logarithmic scale. This means that flipping from one light to two changes the perceived brightness a ton more than going from a 101 to a 102 despite adding the same physical amount of light. Our eyes and brains are simply better at detecting small differences in the absolute brightness of dark scenes and bad at detecting the same differences in bright scenes. Computers and digital image sensors, on the other hand, detect brightness purely based on the number of photons hitting a photo detector. So additional photons register the same increase in brightness regardless of the surrounding scene. When a digital image is stored, the computer just records a brightness value for each color, red, green, and blue, at each point of the image. Typically, zero represents zero brightness and one represents a 100% brightness. So point five is half as bright as one. Right?
cues.zh: 人类的视觉就像我们的听觉一样，是以相对且大致呈对数的尺度运作的。这意味着，将光线从一盏增加到两盏，相比于从 101 盏增加到 102 盏，对感知亮度的改变要巨大得多，尽管它们增加的物理光量是相同的。我们的眼睛和大卫（这里指大脑）只是更善于察觉暗场景中绝对亮度的微小差异，而不擅长察觉亮场景中同样的差异。另一方面，计算机和数码图像传感器纯粹根据撞击光电探测器的光子数量来检测亮度。因此，无论周围场景如何，额外的光子记录的亮度增量都是相同的。当存储数字图像时，计算机只是记录图像每个点上红、绿、蓝三种颜色的亮度值。通常，零代表零亮度，一代表 100% 的亮度。所以零点五的亮度是一的一半。对吧？

cues.en: Nope. This color might look like it's halfway between black and white, but that's because of our logarithmic vision. In terms of absolute physical brightness, it's only one fifth as many photons as white. Even more crazy, an image brightness value of a quarter has just one twentieth of the photons of white. Digital imaging does have a good reason for being designed in this darker than the numbers
cues.zh: 不对。这个颜色看起来可能像是黑白之间的中间色，但那是因为我们的对数视觉。就绝对物理亮度而言，它的光子量只有白色的五分之一。更离谱的是，亮度值为四分之一的图像，其光子量只有白色的二十分之一。数字成像被设计成这种比数值更暗的方式，确实有充分的理由

cues.en: way. Remember, human vision is better at detecting small differences in the brightness of dark scenes, which software engineers took advantage of as a way of saving disk space in the early days of digital imaging. The trick is simple. When a digital camera captures an image, instead of storing the brightness values it gives, store their square roots. This samples the gradations of dark colors with more data points and bright colors with fewer data points, roughly imitating the characteristics of human vision. When you need to display the image on a monitor, just square the brightness back to present the colors properly. This is all well and good until you decide to modify the image file. Blurring, for example, is achieved by replacing each pixel with an average of the colors of nearby pixels. Simple enough. But depending on whether you take the average before or after the square rooting, you'll get different results.
cues.zh: 记住，人类视觉更擅长察觉暗场景亮度的细微差异，软件工程师在数字成像早期就利用这一点来节省磁盘空间。技巧很简单。数码相机捕捉图像时，不存储它给出的亮度值，而是存储这些值的平方根。这样，暗色的渐变用更多数据点采样，亮色用更少数据点采样，大致模仿了人类视觉的特性。当你需要在显示器上显示图像时，只需把亮度平方回去，就能正确呈现颜色。这一切都没问题，直到你决定修改图像文件。比如模糊，是通过把每个像素替换为邻近像素颜色的平均值来实现的。够简单。但取决于你是在取平方根之前还是之后求平均，会得到不同的结果。

cues.en: And unfortunately, the vast majority of computer software does this incorrectly.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，绝大多数计算机软件在这方面都做错了。

cues.en: Like, if you wanna blur a red and green boundary, you'd expect the middle to be half red and half green. And most computers attempt that by lazily averaging the brightness values of the image file, forgetting that the actual brightness values were square rooted by the camera for better data storage. So the average ends up being too dark precisely because an average of two square roots is less than the square root of an average. To correctly blend the red and green and avoid the ugly dark sludge, the computer should have first squared each of the brightnesses to undo the camera's square rooting,
cues.zh: 比如，如果你想模糊红绿边界，你希望中间呈现一半红一半绿。大多数计算机尝试这样做时，只会偷懒地对图像文件的亮度值求平均，却忘了实际的亮度值为了更好地存储数据，已经被相机进行了平方根处理。所以最终的平均值会变得太暗，原因很简单，两个平方根的平均值小于平均值的平方根。要正确地混合红绿色并避免丑陋的暗色污渍，计算机应该首先将每个亮度值平方以撤销相机的平方根处理，

cues.en: then averaged them, and then square rooted it back. Look how much nicer it is. There's actually yellow there. Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 然后求平均值，最后再开平方根。你看现在好看多了。那里真的出现了黄色。遗憾的是，

cues.en: the vast majority of software, ranging from iOS to Instagram to the standard settings in Adobe Photoshop, takes the lazy, ugly, and wrong approach to image brightness. And while there are advanced settings in Photoshop and other professional graphics software that let you use the mathematically and physically correct blending, shouldn't beauty just be the default?
cues.zh: 绝大多数软件，从 iOS 到 Instagram 再到 Adobe Photoshop 的默认设置，在处理图像亮度时都采用了偷懒、丑陋且错误的方法。尽管 Photoshop 和其他专业图形软件中有高级设置允许你使用数学和物理上正确的混合方式，但美观难道不应该成为默认选项吗？
